overview: This Senate resolution supports Red Ribbon Week, held each year from October 23 to 31, a national drug-prevention campaign started in 1988 in memory of Enrique 'Kiki' Camarena, a Drug Enforcement Administration agent killed in the line of duty in 1985. It notes the toll of drug overdoses, especially from fentanyl, and highlights efforts like year-round drop boxes for safely disposing of unused prescription drugs. The resolution encourages Americans to wear red ribbons, light up buildings and landmarks, and take part in drug-prevention activities, and encourages young people to live drug-free. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on October 30, 2025.
for: Supporters say the resolution draws attention to the overdose crisis and encourages families, schools and communities to take part in proven prevention efforts.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or provide any funding for prevention or treatment.
